newsitem.title: EGYPT: U.S. Mideast envoy in Egypt for peace talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mideast envoy in Egypt for peace talks.

text.p: U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross will meet on Saturday Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Egypt for talks on the logjammed Palestinian-Israeli peace process, Egyptian officials said on Friday.
They said Ross will fly from Israel to the Red Sea resort town of Sharm el-Sheikh for talks with Mubarak, who has often mediated in troubled rounds of peace talks.

Israeli-Palestinian peace talks have been stuck since the Jewish state began building a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March. The Palestinians insist Israel suspend settlement activity before resuming peace talks.

Ross's visit to Egypt comes as part of a mission launched by the United States to salvage the peace process. The U.S. envoy met on Friday Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai and was also due to hold another session of talks with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.
On Thursday, Ross said there were difficult problems to solve between the two sides and Palestinian officials said he had not brought any new ideas to restart the talks.

Jordan's King Hussein and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu also met on Thursday to discuss the stalled peace process and on Friday, Jordanian Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawnah held talks with his Egyptian counterpart Amr Moussa on peace moves.
Tarawnah is also due to meet Mubarak on Saturday to deliver a message from the king.
